stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on June 26th.
stocks.news:
Stocks barely moved. The S&P 500 slipped 0.05% to 7,354, the NASDAQ eased 0.24% to 25,297, and the DOW dipped 0.09% to 51,876 (figures as of the June 26th close).

The drama was in the chips. ON Semiconductor (ON -23.66%) had one of its worst days ever after announcing it is buying Synaptics (SYNA -3.68%), a deal it says opens up a $30 billion market in physical AI. Investors apparently wanted to see the receipts first. Meanwhile SpaceX (SPCX +0.15%) is joining the Nasdaq, so millions of index-fund investors are about to own a sliver of a rocket company whether they planned to or not.

economy.note: Stock indexes as of the June 26th close; 10-Year, gold, and Brent as of June 28th (Market Briefs); silver is live spot, June 29th (JM Bullion).
economy.commentary:
Inflation is still running warm. The Federal Reserve's preferred gauge rose 4.1%, the fastest pace since April 2023, and Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin warned it will be tough to cool prices without keeping rates high. Not the update a mortgage shopper was hoping for.

Aluminum went the other way (see the chart below). Prices just logged a fourth straight weekly drop, off 6.4% on the week, as a possible Middle East ceasefire looks set to restart regional supply. Cheaper aluminum could eventually mean cheaper cans, cars, and construction, though builders will believe it when they see it.

Metals were mixed elsewhere: gold eased 0.40% to $4,080 and silver to about $58.80, while Brent crude firmed 0.53% to $73.37 and the 10-year Treasury yield held at 4.38%.

feature_image.alt: LME aluminum price for 2026 year to date in USD per metric ton: a choppy winter between roughly $3,000 and $3,270, a late-February low near $3,030, a spring climb to a mid-June high around $3,750, then a four-week slide to $3,175.62, up 9.6% year to date.
feature_image.caption: Aluminum just notched its fourth straight weekly drop, off 6.4% on the week, as a possible Middle East ceasefire looks set to restart regional supply. Cheaper aluminum could eventually feed through to cheaper cans, cars, and construction costs, a small tailwind for builders if the peace holds.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET, June 28th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto drifted lower. Bitcoin slipped 0.75% to $59,119, still stuck below $60,000, with Ether off 0.82% to $1,557 and XRP down 1.09% to $1.04 (figures as of the June 28th close).

The big money headed for the exits. Investors pulled $1.30 billion from BlackRock's (BLK -0.74%) IBIT last week, 73% of all spot Bitcoin ETF outflows. On the brighter side, Polygon quietly became the busiest network for stablecoin payments, moving $79.25 billion in May as Visa and Meta leaned in, a reminder that the plumbing keeps improving even when prices do not.

real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage Rates Hold At 6.53% As The Fed's Inflation Gauge Runs Hot At 4.1%; Morgan Stanley Says Trading Up Could Double Your Payment; The East Bay Board Eases To 2,945 Active On 230 New And 190 Closed
real_estate.commentary:
The 30-year fixed held at 6.53% and the 15-year at 6.12%. With the Fed's inflation gauge still hot, the gentle drift lower we have seen is likely to stay gentle, and the lock-in effect thinning resale supply is not loosening its grip.

Morgan Stanley put a number on the standoff. A homeowner who sold today and bought a similar home could see their monthly payment jump about 200%, roughly $1,300 to $1,400 more a month. That math is exactly why so many owners are staying put.

At the luxury end, sellers are getting creative. With fewer cash buyers around, some are accepting private tech-company stock instead of cash, including a $2.6 million Miami listing taking startup shares. Hard to value and harder to resell, but in a slow market a willing buyer is a willing buyer.

Locally, the East Bay board eased to 2,945 active (down 19 from Friday), with 230 new listings against 190 closings. Oakland again led the board with 42 new on 778 active; Fremont added 28 new on 355 active.

New-listing flow came in at 230, led by Oakland (42), Fremont (28), and Dublin (23). Closings totaled 190.

For agents: the Fed's hot inflation read is a reminder not to promise buyers a quick rate cut. Lean into the fresh supply (2,945 active, 230 new) and price discipline. Well-priced, well-presented homes still sell inside about four weeks, while overpriced listings just sit, so the coaching stays the same: price to today's market and the sale follows.
